scheme_name: Coffee Development Programme in North Eastern Region: Quality Upgradation / Certification: Support for Eco-Certification / Organic Certification
description:
The Coffee Development Programme in the North Eastern Region of India is a significant initiative aimed at enhancing the quality and sustainability of coffee production in this region. 

This program was launched in 2005 under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. 

The primary objective of the program is to promote the cultivation of high-quality coffee. 

It aims to increase the income of coffee farmers by providing them with the necessary support for quality upgradation and certification. 

The program specifically targets the states of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, and Tripura. 

These states have a unique potential for coffee cultivation due to their climatic conditions and biodiversity. 

The program focuses on achieving measurable targets such as increasing the area under coffee cultivation by 20 percent by 2025. 

Additionally, it aims to enhance the productivity of coffee plantations by at least 30 percent within the same timeframe. 

One of the key benefits of the Coffee Development Programme is the financial assistance provided to farmers. 

Farmers can receive up to INR 1 lakh per hectare for the establishment of new coffee plantations. 

This financial support is crucial for small and marginal farmers who may lack the capital to invest in coffee cultivation. 

The program also provides assistance for quality upgradation through training and capacity-building initiatives. 

Farmers are trained in best practices for coffee cultivation, including pest management, soil health, and post-harvest processing. 

The program emphasizes the importance of eco-certification and organic certification for coffee produced in the region. 

Farmers are supported in obtaining certifications that can enhance the marketability of their coffee. 

This includes financial assistance for the certification process which can be substantial. 

The cost of obtaining organic certification can range from INR 50,000 to INR 1 lakh depending on the size of the farm and the certification body. 

The eligibility criteria for farmers to participate in the program include being a resident of one of the target states. 

Farmers must also have a minimum of 1 hectare of land for coffee cultivation. 

Additionally, they should be engaged in coffee farming for at least three years. 

The application process for the Coffee Development Programme involves several steps. 

Farmers must first approach the local Coffee Board office or the designated implementing agency in their state. 

They are required to fill out an application form that includes details about their land and previous coffee cultivation experience. 

Documents required for the application include proof of land ownership, identity proof, and any previous certifications if applicable. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by officials from the Coffee Board. 

Farmers may be required to undergo a field inspection to verify the details provided in the application. 

If approved, farmers will receive a letter of sanction detailing the financial assistance and support they will receive. 

The disbursement of funds is typically made in installments based on the progress of the coffee plantation. 

The first installment is usually released after the initial setup of the plantation is verified. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the achievement of specific milestones. 

The program also includes periodic evaluations to assess the impact of the assistance provided. 

These evaluations help in refining the program and ensuring that it meets the needs of the farmers effectively. 

The implementing authority for the Coffee Development Programme is the Coffee Board of India. 

The Coffee Board operates under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. 

Farmers can contact the Coffee Board through their official website or local offices for more information. 

The program has seen a significant increase in participation since its inception. 

As of 2023, over 10,000 farmers have benefited from the program across the North Eastern states. 

The program has also contributed to the establishment of over 5,000 hectares of new coffee plantations. 

This has resulted in an estimated increase in coffee production by 15 percent in the region. 

The Coffee Development Programme also focuses on promoting sustainable farming practices. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt organic farming methods that reduce the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides. 

This not only improves the quality of coffee but also benefits the environment. 

The program has also facilitated the establishment of farmer cooperatives. 

These cooperatives help farmers in collective marketing of their produce. 

This ensures better prices for their coffee and reduces the influence of middlemen. 

The program has also initiated awareness campaigns about the benefits of eco-certification. 

Farmers are educated about the premium prices that certified organic coffee can fetch in the market. 

The Coffee Development Programme is aligned with the government's broader goals of promoting sustainable agriculture. 

It supports the national agenda of increasing farmers' incomes and enhancing rural livelihoods. 

The program has received positive feedback from participants who have reported increased yields and better market access. 

In conclusion, the Coffee Development Programme in the North Eastern Region is a comprehensive initiative. 

It addresses the challenges faced by coffee farmers through financial assistance, training, and certification support. 

The program plays a crucial role in promoting the economic development of the region. 

It aims to transform the North Eastern states into significant players in the global coffee market. 

The focus on quality upgradation and sustainability is expected to yield long-term benefits for the farmers and the environment. 

Farmers interested in the program should act promptly to take advantage of the available support. 

The program is a testament to the Indian government's commitment to enhancing the livelihoods of coffee farmers in the North East. 

Through this initiative, the potential of the region's coffee industry is being realized. 

The Coffee Development Programme is not just about coffee cultivation. 

It is about empowering farmers and creating a sustainable future for coffee production in India.
